newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates firm on mills' demand.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates firm on mills' demand.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates firmed on Monday on a slightly higher demand from mills having export orders for yarn and cloth, dealers said.
The mills were buying at a higher price as they had export orders for yarn and cloth, which fetch good prices in world markets, dealer Nasim Usman said.
All the three main varieties quoted by the private Karachi Cotton Association (KCA) in its daily official spot rates rose 27.50 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) each, Usman said.
In the kerb market, the NIAB-78 variety was traded at 2,400 rupees per maund.
